note: BLOCKED -- no __items.csv written. The study's own questionnaire appendix (Additional file 4 of Mekheimer & Abdelhalim, 'Beyond translation', Asian-Pacific J. Second & Foreign Lang. Educ., doi:10.1186/s40862-025-00378-1, file 40862_2025_378_MOESM4_ESM.docx, figshare 31387855, CC BY 4.0) DOES publish the full wording: 'Perceived Academic Freedom (PAF) Scale', instructions 'Please indicate how much you agree or disagree with the following statements about your academic freedom.', Section 1 Research Autonomy (5 statements) and Section 2 Teaching & Expressive Freedom (5 statements), on a printed 5-anchor Strongly Disagree..Strongly Agree grid. The block is not an availability failure: the wording cannot be soundly attached to the live item codes PAF_1..PAF_10, for three independent reasons, all re-runnable via verify_mekheimer_2026_paf.R (VERDICT: PASS). (1) RESP SCALE CONTRADICTION: the live table stores resp 1..7 while the appendix grid prints five anchors; 375 of 1600 stored responses (23.4%) sit above the top printed anchor, so no published anchor set maps onto resp and option_text would have to be blank or invented. (2) THE PAPER'S OWN DESCRIPTIVES CONTRADICT THE COLUMN LABELS: Additional file 2 (40862_2025_378_MOESM2_ESM.xlsx, N=496) tabulates every questionnaire item as q1..q38 with subtotals that reproduce exactly, fixing PAF = q1..q10 (published means 4.2 4.0 3.8 4.1 3.9 4.0 3.8 3.5 3.4 3.9; sections 20.0 / 18.5, total 38.5). Live PAF_1..PAF_10 means are 4.53 4.91 4.14 5.11 3.67 4.29 5.14 4.58 4.54 4.91 (sections 22.4 / 23.5, total 45.8) and match NO 10-wide window of q1..q38 -- rmse 0.8661 against their own q1..q10 and 0.8102 at the best of 29 windows. The same deposit's sibling CAI_* columns were shown in batch_287 to be shifted +4 against the same q series, so the deposit's column labelling is demonstrably unreliable rather than merely unverified. (3) DATA DEFECT: PAF_7 = PAF_3 + 1 for all 160 respondents exactly (cor 1.000000000000, a single distinct difference value). Two distinct instrument statements cannot stand in a deterministic affine relation over every respondent, so at least one of those two codes does not carry the responses to the statement its position implies. Inter-item |r| is 0.83-1.00 across the other nine, which is the corpus-trust duplication signature rather than a plausible design. The one corroborating signal -- PAF_5 is the table's sole negatively-keyed item (mean r -0.88 against the other nine), matching the appendix's Section 1 item 5 '(R)' reverse marker -- pins one position and cannot rescue the other nine. STEP 3b NAME MISMATCH (log for the dictionary, independent of the block): the IRW dictionary Description reads 'Professional Academic Functioning scale'; the instrument is the study's 'Perceived Academic Freedom (PAF) Scale'. Same 10 items, wrong expansion of the acronym. RIGHTS: no bar. The PAF scale is the study's own instrument, published in its own CC BY 4.0 article appendix; the figshare deposit is CC BY (licence value 52, https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); no fee, permission-required, non-commercial, no-derivatives or no-redistribution clause is stated on the deposit record or in the appendix, and there is no Perceived Academic Freedom row in itemtext/instrument_rights_register.csv. RETRY TEST: NO. An unchanged retry reproduces this exactly -- the sources were all fetched successfully and the verdict is determinate, resting on a data defect that makes the item text unattachable. It would take a corrected deposit (columns on the published 5-point scale, PAF_3/PAF_7 de-duplicated, means reconciling with Additional file 2) or an author clarification of the column labelling to change the outcome.
